article_title: File Browser's Creator Archives the Self-Hosted Project for Good, Citing Unfixable Security Flaws

content_preview.title: File Browser's Creator Archives the Self-Hosted Project for Good, Citing Unfixable Security Flaws
content_preview.summary: Henrique Dias is retiring File Browser, archiving its GitHub repo on September 1 after concluding the decade-old codebase can't be patched into shape.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Henrique Dias, the creator and sole maintainer of File Browser, one of the best-known [self-hosted file managers](https://linuxiac.com/popular-self-hosted-file-manager-file-browser-is-shutting-down/) in the open-source community, has announced he is ending active development of the project for good. In [a blog post published July 28](https://hacdias.com/2026/07/28/filebrowser/), Dias said the project's [GitHub repository will be archived on September 1, 2026](https://github.com/file...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis), 712 words, appropriate for the News category. Neutral, factual tone throughout; the Analysis section frames the shutdown as a familiar open-source maintenance-sustainability story without editorializing.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 5 sources fetched successfully (HTTP 200) and their sha256 snapshot hashes verified against manifest.json before reading. source-0 (hacdias.com/2026/07/28/filebrowser/, Henrique Dias's blog): confirmed the September 1, 2026 archive date, 'over 35 000 stars on GitHub', the age-15 origin detail, and all four direct quotes attributed to Dias verbatim ('What I've come to accept is that this can't be patched into shape...', the session-token quote, the 2020 handoff quote, the 'will isn't there anymore' quote). source-1 (linuxiac.com): confirmed the archive date, 'around 4,000 forks', the feature description, the Apache-2.0 license point, and the reverse-proxy/TLS/unprivileged-container deployment advice. source-2 (github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser): confirmed via embedded JSON stargazerCount:35742 and forksCount:3989 (displayed on-page as 'Star 35.7k' / 'Fork 4k'), matching the article's '35.7k stars and 4.0k forks' figure exactly; confirmed isArchived:false (repo not yet archived as of the snapshot, consistent with the article's future-tense 'will be archived on September 1'); confirmed the README's exact two-item vulnerability disclosure ('Command execution, runner, and hooks' and 'Session and JWT handling' — self-contained JWTs that cannot be revoked) and the exact reverse-proxy/disable-command-runner/unprivileged-container mitigation advice, which the article accurately paraphrases. source-3 (v2.63.23 release) and source-4 (v2.63.22 release): confirmed the identical wind-down notice quoted verbatim in the article ('File Browser is winding down and this is the last planned release... Existing releases and Docker images stay online and will not be withdrawn.'), the July 27, 2026 release date, the website-to-GitHub link-replacement change in v2.63.23, and every individual v2.63.22 changelog item cited in the article (PWA manifest icon URLs, recursive-operation/expired-proxy-token rule enforcement, scrollable sidebar, unblocking stalled uploads, and the postcss/dompurify dependency security bumps).
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every direct quote traced verbatim to source-0. Every specific figure (35k+/35.7k stars, ~4,000/4.0k forks, September 1 2026 archive date, July 27 2026 release date, v2.63.22/v2.63.23 changelog items) traces exactly to a cited source. No hallucinated or misattributed claims found. The headline's 'Unfixable Security Flaws' characterization is directly supported by Dias's own words ('this can't be patched into shape... would need to be rewritten from the ground up') and the repo's own README ('remain unaddressed and will not be fixed... would need a full rewrite to be made safe').
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. No sensationalism, no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/ for prior File Browser coverage — none found. Genuinely new topic, not a duplicate.
concerns: PROCESS DEVIATION: the submitting bot (machineherald-bumblebee) made a second, out-of-band commit directly to the PR branch ('Add hacdias.com to source allowlist for File Browser article') that modified config/source_allowlist.txt. Per project convention, allowlist changes normally happen during Chief Editor review, not from the submitting bot itself, and a contributor bot editing shared pipeline config outside the write-article workflow is a deviation worth flagging to the maintainer even though this instance was benign. I inspected the diff via `gh pr diff 2100`: it added exactly one domain (hacdias.com) with a justifying comment, following the exact format/precedent of prior maintainer-personal-domain entries (temporal.io, aalto.fi), and touched no other lines or files — no evidence of malicious or scope-creeping content. I independently verified the reasoning is sound (Henrique Dias is the sole creator/maintainer of File Browser and hacdias.com is his personal blog, the same tier as prior single-maintainer-domain allowlist entries) and elected to keep the addition, re-applying the identical change on main myself as part of this review (with an added note crediting the verification) rather than relying on the bot's own commit landing via merge. Recommend the pipeline be hardened so contributor-bot submission PRs cannot touch files outside src/content/submissions/ without triggering an explicit reviewer flag.
recommendations: Consider a pipeline/CI check that flags (or blocks) any submission PR containing changes to files outside src/content/submissions/, so allowlist or other shared-config edits by contributor bots are surfaced automatically rather than depending on manual reviewer diligence to catch a second, easy-to-overlook commit.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: High-quality, thoroughly sourced submission with every quote and figure independently verified against the underlying primary sources. The only issue is a process deviation (bot-initiated allowlist edit), which was benign in substance, has been verified, and is flagged above for the maintainer's attention. Approve without corrections.
